title: Ramadan: the Night of Power
hookLine: a night better than a thousand months, sought in the last ten (97:1–5)
tomorrow: Ramadan: the fast of the tongue
last: TARAWIH — THE NIGHTS ARE FOR STANDING.

cards: A thousand months is about eighty-three years. A whole lifetime, most of one anyway. Somewhere in the next ten nights there's one night worth more than all of that.
Nobody says which. Only that it's one of them, probably an odd one. What would anyone do?
In the last ten nights of Ramadan, the answer is easy to see: stay up, show up, try not to miss it. Mosques stay full past midnight. Some people don't go home at all.

teach.b: It's called Laylat al-Qadr. Laylah is night. Qadr is harder to translate: power, measure, decree, worth.

Pickthall calls it the Night of Power. It has its own short surah, al-Qadr, five verses. It says this was the night the Qur'an was sent down, then asks: what will make you understand what the Night of Power is?
And answers: "The Night of Power is better than a thousand months." The angels and the Spirit come down in it, by their Lord's permission, and it is peace until the rising of the dawn.
So Muslims remember it as the night the revelation began, the night in the cave of Hira you met back in camp two. But which night?

teach.h: SEEK IT IN THE ODD NIGHTS.
teach.b: A hadith in Bukhari says seek it in the odd nights of the last ten: the twenty-first, twenty-third, twenty-fifth, twenty-seventh, twenty-ninth. Some give special weight to the twenty-seventh, others to other nights.
And there's a story about why nobody knows for sure. In Bukhari, the Prophet ﷺ came out one night to tell the people which night it was.

teach.h: TAKEN UP, BECAUSE OF A QUARREL.
teach.b: On the way, he found two men quarreling, and the knowledge was taken up from him. He told them: perhaps that is better for you. So the not-knowing became part of the gift: people seek it on all ten.
And Aisha once asked him: if I find it, what should I say?

teach.h: ON THAT NIGHT, ASK FOR PARDON.
teach.b: He taught her a short line, in Tirmidhi, that asks God, who loves to pardon, to pardon her. Not wealth. Not success.
Pardon. On the night worth a lifetime, that was the request.

how: In the last ten nights of Ramadan, Muslims seek Laylat al-Qadr with extra prayer, Qur'an recitation and supplication, especially on the odd nights and often the twenty-seventh, and some stay in the mosque in retreat (i'tikaf).

the night a new Islamic year begins

the Qur'an says it's better than a thousand months

games.q: the Prophet ﷺ is on his way to tell everyone which night is the Night of Power. he passes two men quarreling. what happens?
o: the knowledge is taken up, and he says perhaps that's better for you
he stops to settle the quarrel first
games.why: the knowledge was lifted, and he told them to seek it in the last ten; perhaps that is better for you (Bukhari).

practice: Before you sleep, sit up in bed or on the floor, lights low, for one minute of quiet you wouldn't have had.
If you pray, pray a little more, or ask for pardon the way Aisha was taught; if you don't, simply sit, and let it be a night you didn't let slip past.
You don't know which night matters most, so the minute belongs to every one of them.

wordCard.voice: Laylat al-Qadr. The Night of Power, when the Qur'an was first sent down, better than a thousand months, sought in the last ten nights. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the Night of Power (or of measure, decree); the name of Surah 97.

carryVoice: Your line: better than a thousand months. Ten nights, and one of them is it. See you tomorrow.
